newsitem.title: USA: Lot cargo exports via JFK up sharply in June.
newsitem.headline: Lot cargo exports via JFK up sharply in June.

text.p: Lot Polish Airlines handled 181 tonnes of outbound commercial freight at John F. Kennedy airport in June, up 52 percent from 119 tonnes in same 1996 month, Margaret Budnica, cargo sales manager for the carrier's JFK station, told Reuters.
The import side was a bit weaker. Lot imported 120 tonnes of freight into the New York area via JFK in June, down 23 percent from 156 tonnes a year earlier.
Budnica attributed the decline of inbound cargo to added traffic forwarded to Newark International Airport in New Jersey.
When asked how much of the overall decline in imports at JFK was attributable to imports forwarded to Newark, Budnica said, "All of it and then some."
She explained that one client shipping 15 tonnes per month to New York opted to send its entire shipment via Newark in June.
Budnica said there was not enough space to accommodate the forwarder's shipment at JFK and the client preferred to not have the freight separated between the two stations.

The Lot official said the 52 percent increase of cargo tonnage exported from JFK in June was entirely due to rate adjustments the carrier implemented in the beginning of Summer. She said the rates were at least 60 percent lower than what they had been.
The actual rates, she said, would not be publishable. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
